items.summary: The S&P 500 ended lower on Nov 2 after oil prices fell amid optimism over a possible US-Iran peace deal. Apple shares dipped 1.5% before its report, which then beat expectations but left the stock near flat. Separately, Palantir slipped 3.1% and AMD fell 7.5% ahead of their reports on Nov 3, as investors weighed AI spending concerns amid US midterm elections that day.
items.title: S&P 500 Falls as Apple Dips Before Earnings

items.summary: On Nov 2, Anthropic reported more than an 1,100 per cent surge in quarterly revenue to US$17 billion from US$1.4 billion the prior year, alongside nearly US$900 billion in spending commitments ahead of its November Wall Street listing. The filing also disclosed a net loss of US$23.3 billion and an operating loss of US$567 million as it paid more for computing capacity.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals a dramatic revenue jump amid AI spending worries

items.summary: Matt Scherer, co-author of the report Brace for Impact, argues in an opinion piece dated Nov 2, 2026 that the Securities and Exchange Commission should block Anthropic’s initial public offering. He contends that AI companies’ finances are murky due to circular business dealings and heavy financial engineering. Footnotes reportedly revealed nearly $900 billion in spending commitments stretching into the 2030s, while the company’s 2026 results remain unaudited. Scherer notes revenue growth slowed over summer 2026, with one study finding Americans using AI at work fell from 46% in 2025 to 33% in 2026. He asserts that competition and high data center costs—estimated at $31 billion per gigawatt—will pressure margins. Scherer calls for two consecutive quarters of audited financials before the debut, warning otherwise workers and investors could be left exposed as off-balance-sheet debts come due.
items.title: Commentator Urges SEC to Block Anthropic IPO Over Financial Risks

items.summary: NVIDIA presents Cosmos, a platform of world foundation models and development tools aimed at physical AI developers facing challenges in adapting models to sensors, tasks, and data. The offering includes the Cosmos Framework with agent skills and training recipes, plus NIM microservices for GPU-accelerated inference serving across autonomous vehicle, robotics, and surgical simulation scenarios.
items.title: NVIDIA Cosmos Framework for Physical AI World Models

items.summary: Databricks announced that Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud, letting teams run production-grade, serverless Postgres directly on the Databricks Data + AI Platform. The architecture separates compute from storage and shares one storage layer with analytical data to cut overhead and cost of ownership as part of its LTAP model. KaBuM! selected it for low-latency reads and writes powering conversational AI.
items.title: Databricks Makes Lakebase Postgres Generally Available on Google Cloud

items.summary: While reviewing Anthropic’s revised S-1A filing, attention turned to a warning in its Risk Factors section that the company appears close to recursive self-improvement (RSI). The lab stated it uses AI in research and cautioned that this could accelerate progress faster than safety measures can keep pace. It noted none of its current models have crossed RSI’s threshold yet and plans updates to its Responsible Scaling Policy to retain human supervision over frontier model development.
items.title: Anthropic flags nearness to self-building AI

items.summary: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus is reportedly advancing household robot development, with the first product possibly being an autonomous home robot that supports FaceTime calls and controls lights. People who worked on Apple’s robotic projects told The Information it could be named HomeView Ultra, code-named J595, priced at $1,000 or more by 2027—though delays may push the launch to 2028. Critics note its reported features seem underwhelming versus existing smart home devices.
items.title: Apple’s New CEO Pushes a $1,000 Home Robot Targeting 2027

items.summary: Last week Anthropic introduced a system prompt to stop its Claude models from recreating specific existing video games. A social media user named chasm reported the change around October 27, and XDA later verified it appears in version 2.1.314 of the Claude Code binary released on October 30. Anthropic engineer Addy Osmani confirmed two sentences were added to steer away from recreating others' games.
items.title: Anthropic's new game-cloning rule may not curb AI copying boom

items.summary: The MIT Energy Initiative held its annual research conference on Sept. 22-23 under the theme “Transitioning energy at a pivotal moment,” drawing more than 200 attendees in person and online. Paula Hammond opened by stressing that the energy transition requires an interdisciplinary and international approach, while keynote speaker Eric Toone framed prosperity as tied to emissions yet pointed to zero-carbon technologies such as iron-air batteries. Sessions covered nuclear revival, carbon utilization, quantum sensing, startup commercialization and data-center growth; Steve Clemmer cited a recent analysis showing new facilities could be 10 to even 10,000 times larger than those from a decade ago. Speakers emphasized earning community trust amid rising opposition.
items.title: MIT Energy Initiative Conference Explores Decarbonization, AI and Quantum Tools

items.summary:
Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE malware botnet of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes that Google says its manufacturer intentionally infected to generate revenue through cybercrime. The company attributes the infection with high confidence to Chinese maker Videostrong Technology Co, accusing it of installing a persistent backdoor into device firmware and selling access to criminal affiliates used for ad fraud, residential proxies, and other malware. Google terminated its relationship with Videostrong, revoked its license to manufacture certified Android devices, and banned future affiliates from producing them. Synthient traced the malware after finding it preinstalled on a MECOOL box purchased in late 2025. Although operations were disrupted, the backdoor remains on infected devices unless clean firmware is installed or they are disconnected online.

visual null
items.title: Google Takedowns Million-Device XCPE Android Botnet, Bans TV Box Maker

items.summary: During Halloween weekend, some Grok Bot users saw their weekly usage limits jump to 100%, a change Musk confirmed on X was not a glitch. He said serving costs were unsustainably high relative to revenue. The agentic AI is central to SpaceX's newly public business, where AI now accounts for 52% of income and its Super Intelligence division reported $431 million profit before $1.2 billion in one-time Cursor acquisition costs.
items.title: Musk Cuts Grok Bot Limits Over Unsustainable Costs

items.summary: Ray announced today a new Special Interest Group (SIG) dedicated to hardware accelerators, marking what the announcement calls a crucial time to build on Ray's foundation. When Ray was created at UC Berkeley over 10 years ago, distributed computing meant CPU clusters running frameworks like Apache Hadoop and Spark; GPUs were only just entering machine learning. Today accelerated computing is central to AI development and deployment. The public interest group will bring together hardware vendors, contributors, and developers to define a shared, vendor-neutral roadmap covering three core areas: Development and Testing Infrastructure, Hardware Awareness Capabilities, and Networking/Transport.
items.title: Ray Announces Special Interest Group for Hardware Accelerators

items.summary: Google published a roundup of its most recent artificial intelligence news from October 2026. The company said it has invested in machine learning and AI research for more than 20 years to build products that improve everyday life. In the month, Google released Gemini 4 Argon, described as a frontier reasoning model available globally across several platforms, then announced Gemini 4 Carbon two weeks later as its strongest cybersecurity and long-horizon engineering model yet; Carbon is in pre-release testing with U. S. government partners through the Fairwind Program before a broader launch.
items.title: Google Reviews Its October AI Announcements Across Models, Safety and Research

items.summary: Ai2's Olmo 3 earned the highest ethical rating from open-source platform Nextcloud, which calls it green. The company requires its supported models to use open-source training and inference software, let users self-host a trained model, and expose publicly available training data so people can inspect how a model was built and reproduce it. This aligns with Nextcloud's goal of reducing dependence on big tech while keeping AI transparent and controllable through llm2, its local LLM backend. Marcel Klehr, a software engineer at Nextcloud, said Olmo 3 was a natural choice for these reasons. The model also runs well on consumer hardware without high-end GPUs, fitting the needs of public-sector agencies like CSIC, which serves roughly 17,000 researchers with a self-hosted environment.
items.title: Olmo 3 Achieves Nextcloud's Highest Ethical AI Rating

items.summary: In a Forum piece titled 'Make local vegetables affordable at places where consumers shop,' Liu Fook Thim notes that SG Farmers' Market vending machines will sell lettuce and nai bai for $1.40 to $1.80 a pack, compared with at least $2 leafy greens at FairPrice (Oct 28). He argues the real benchmark is imported produce prices, warns more machines do not guarantee sales, and calls for supply-chain cost cuts so local vegetables are consistently affordable where consumers already shop.
items.title: Commentator questions cost of local vegetable vending machines

items.summary: Regina Barzilay and James Collins of MIT received the 2026 Pritzker Prize for AI in Science Research Excellence for pioneering AI-enabled antibiotic discovery. Their work, including identifying halicin through a deep learning model trained on 2,500 molecules, accelerated drug-resistant bacteria research from years to weeks. Both researchers emphasized that AI automates parts of discovery rather than fully transforming it.
items.title: MIT Researchers Win Pritzker Prize for AI Antibiotic Discovery Work

items.summary: This explainer describes how Nvidia built its Nemotron family of large language models, focusing on techniques that reduce computation and memory. The article states the model combines Mamba layers with a mixture-of-experts architecture inside one transformer network, using only some parameters per token while keeping roughly 30 billion total parameters but activating about 3 billion for each token. It also notes Nvidia uses grouped-query attention (32 query heads versus 2 key-value heads), BF16 weights at 16 bits, and the NVFP4 format with quantization-aware distillation to shrink storage from approx. 66 GB in BF16 to approx. 22 GB for the checkpoint. The piece reports Nemotron 3 Super has approx. 120 billion total parameters and 12 billion active ones, while a later Ultra model scales this to 550 billion total and 55 billion active. Details are drawn from publicly shared sources.
items.title: Nvidia Explains How Nemotron Cuts Model Costs

items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, prompting concern about the security of internet-connected devices. Experts say manufacturers must improve device safety, while UK law now requires certain smart-device makers to meet minimum standards since April 2024.
items.title: Suspected cyber-attack on European supermarket fridges raises wider hardware-security fears

items.summary: Tesla has launched Heat Pump Optimization, a feature on the Powerwall 3 and three-phase Powerwall 3P that signals compatible heat pumps to run harder so homes can store cheap or surplus solar energy as hot water. It is live in Europe only; Tesla has not commented on US or Canada rollout. The feature relies on SG-Ready certification introduced by the German Heat Pump Association (BWP) in 2012, and requires specific firmware versions plus physical wiring installed by a certified installer. Tesla Energy summarized it on X: “Heat Pump Optimization allows your Powerwall to boost heating when there’s surplus solar or energy is inexpensive.” A 300-liter tank heated an extra 30°C holds about 10.5 kWh, needing around 3.5 kWh at COP of 3, leaving the Powerwall's 13.5 kWh free for other loads.
items.title: Tesla Rolls Out Heat Pump Optimization for Powerwall 3 in Europe

items.summary: Two new reports argue that a methane measurement method called global warming potential, or GWP*, lets livestock-heavy countries hide real emissions. A Greenpeace-commissioned analysis of the top 10 livestock exporters found they could cut actual methane by only 0.6 percent yet report a 30 percent reduction under GWP*. The gap equals about 1,538 million metric tons of carbon dioxide in one year. Separately, researchers at UCLA found beef meals measured as roughly 3,500 grams under the standard method but more than 7,000 grams over 20 years. Campaigners call it creative accounting that weakens climate goals.
items.title: Greenpeace Report Criticizes GWP* Methane Accounting

items.summary: BMW is ending US sales of the iX after a four-year run, with 2026 models essentially sold out. The landing page now redirects to the gas-powered X5 while an electric replacement, the iX5, arrives in early 2027. CarsDirect reports about 10 new iX models remain nationwide. BMW says it will open orders this month starting at $79,800 and begin production at Plant Spartanburg by year's end.
items.title: BMW Discontinues iX as Electric X5 Replacement Nears

items.summary: Carbon Brief has produced an interactive table analysing around 100 documents on positions ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. The site notes Australia leads negotiations while Turkey hosts and pushes its own action agenda covering electrification, oceans and green industrialisation. Topics include a just transition mechanism agreed at COP30 but still lacking details, contested climate finance under Article 9.1, adaptation versus mitigation priorities, and nationally determined contributions. As of the writing, only 150 parties responsible for three-quarters of global emissions have submitted new NDCs by 2025, while a joint letter from 105 parties called for putting oceans at the heart of climate action. The table is described as a living document to be updated over COP31.
items.title: Carbon Brief Maps Positions Ahead of COP31 Climate Talks

items.summary: Scott Childers, vice president of Industry & Technology at Stryten Energy, argues that grid resilience requires more than simply adding generation capacity. As demand rises from data centers, manufacturing and electrification, the challenge is delivering power where and when it is needed. New generation does not necessarily resolve transmission constraints or short periods of extreme demand, placing a premium on flexibility. Childers says energy storage can provide this at multiple points across the system, but its full value depends on moving beyond treating storage as one asset class. Different grid challenges require different response times and durations; he notes that no single battery chemistry will win, so combinations should be matched to each application's specific needs.
items.title: Stryten Energy Argues Grid Resilience Needs More Than Added Capacity

items.summary: Oilprice.com's Michael Kern presents four energy stocks positioned across three midterm scenarios, noting prediction markets priced a Democratic sweep at about 71 percent as of the writing. The picks favor companies insulated from Congress or grid policy: Bloom Energy supplies its own power for data centers; NextEra and Dominion pursue a $67 billion merger Virginia regulators must decide within six months of the July 15 filing; Cheniere raised EBITDA guidance citing wartime pricing tied to netbacks more than doubling; Texas Pacific Land owns close to 900,000 acres in West Texas. Kern frames Republican gridlock as favoring status-quo businesses while governors and commissions retain independent power over data center approvals.
items.title: Four Energy Stocks Tied to Midterm Election Outcomes

items.summary: Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations, driven by early demand for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. Fourth-quarter sales were $114.48 billion versus estimates of $113.39 billion, per LSEG data, while profit was $2.10 per share above the $1.99 estimate even excluding tariff refunds. Price increases on older iPhones and Macs helped offset rising memory-chip costs, though supply constraints remain on the foldable iPhone Duo with no timeline for balance.
items.title: Apple beats forecasts as iPhone sales and price rises hold up

items.summary: Apple reported strong revenue growth Monday, driven by sustained demand for its smartphones during CEO John Ternus' first earnings call. The company cited soaring memory costs as a factor behind a $100 price increase on iPhones. Analysts noted Apple's conservative AI approach has let it outpace peers like the Mag 7 amid tech volatility.
items.title: Apple Beats Revenue Estimates in CEO Ternus' First Earnings Call

items.summary: On Monday, Anthropic reported a more than 1,100 per cent surge in quarterly revenue as it prepares to go public on Wall Street later this month. Its listing is expected as early as next week amid investor nervousness about AI spending. The company said its net loss reached US$23.3 billion and committed to spend about US$895 billion, mostly over the next five years.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Revenue Surge Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Amazon listed a 128GB iPhone 16 at ₹76,999, down from an MRP of Rs 89,900, giving a direct discount of ₹12,901 or roughly 14%. Additional offers may lower the effective cost further: up to ₹5,000 off with HDFC Bank credit cards and cashback of up to ₹2,309 through Amazon Pay Balance. However, these benefits may not all combine, and final savings depend on buyer eligibility and the exchanged phone's condition.
items.title: Amazon's iPhone 16 Diwali deal hides extra savings in fine print

items.summary: This NBER Working Paper by Babbar, Kantor, Whalley, and Zeng examines how public research spending shaped automation during the Cold War-era Space Race. Using patent data from 1947 to 1992, they find NASA-sponsored patents were more automation-intensive than comparable non-NASA patents, and that industries exposed to space activity saw persistent labor share declines with little change in skill composition. The authors conclude mission-oriented public R&D can redirect technological change with lasting distributional effects.
items.title: NASA R&D Drove Automation in US Manufacturing During Space Race

items.summary: David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein and Joao Guerreiro study optimal monetary policy in a heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian economy. Rather than maximizing a social welfare function, the policymaker maximizes the joint surplus of all households without taking a distributional stance. Departures from the representative-agent benchmark arise from heterogeneous labor wedges, which raise the weight on output-gap stabilization by about 37 percent.
items.title: Baqaee, Burstein and Guerreiro propose surplus-maximizing monetary policy

items.summary: A new survey by The Business Council of Norfolk Island examines the difficulties businesses face operating in a remote Australian territory, from freight and insurance costs to commercial systems built for mainland Australia. Of 239 businesses contacted, 103 responded, with nearly half reporting worsening conditions over the past year; long-established firms were especially affected, with 27 of 42 reporting deterioration versus four of 21 newer ones. Freight was cited by 70% of respondents as a concern, followed by insurance at 45%. The author notes that older businesses developed under different arrangements and may face additional adaptation costs, though sector, size and market conditions could also contribute. Among employers, 41% reported adverse effects from laws or policies compared with 7% of sole operators.
items.title: Norfolk Island Businesses Struggle with Remote-Island Systems

items.summary: British Gas has resumed force-fitting prepay meters in homes of customers unable to afford bills, months after paying the largest energy settlement on record. The regulator lifted a block dating back almost four years that had stopped clawing back unpaid debts through meter fittings following the 2022 scandal amid the Russian gas crisis. Forced fittings remain banned for households with young children or people over 75.
items.title: British Gas resumes force-fitting prepay meters after £112m settlement

items.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood scaled back her strictest migration plans following a cabinet backlash, offering care workers an exemption to apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years. Most other rigorous changes remain, including long waits of up to 30 years for those arriving by irregular means. Home Office officials estimate about 500,000 migrants will wait longer than the current five years, though critics note 1.4 million out of 1.9 million 'Boriswave' legal migrants would still qualify after five years. The Law Society and business groups warned the retrospective rules could undermine certainty and cost businesses. Andy Burnham endorsed the earned-element approach while opposition figures condemned it as capitulation.
items.title: Mahmood softens immigration settlement rules after cabinet revolt

items.summary: Major automakers urged US lawmakers to ban Chinese vehicle imports after midterm elections, as Beijing's car companies expand internationally. A representative cited Europe—where China's industrial overcapacity is blamed for job losses—as a cautionary tale. BYD reported higher sales for a sixth straight month on exports; Geely's overseas sales more than doubled amid 1% overall delivery growth while domestic demand weakens.
items.title: US Automakers Urge Ban on Chinese Vehicle Imports After Midterms

items.summary: An unnamed reader says both *Fjord* and *Fatherland* were worth watching. *Fjord*, by Romanian director Cristian Mungiu, won the Golden Prize at Cannes about family versus state rights in raising children; the reviewer found it right-wing and heavy-handed but noted critics still debate his stance. *Fatherland*, a Polish film on postwar Germany following Thomas Mann's daughter Erika (1h22m), was called convincing yet demanding of German history knowledge.
items.title: A viewer weighs two films on rights and history

items.summary: A study by Grant Thornton Bharat and Entrust Family Office finds that only 36% of wealthy Indian families have a documented succession plan, while another 42% rely on informal arrangements. The researchers note that agreement among family members does not ensure clarity over roles or decision-making authority during leadership transitions.
items.title: Few Wealthy Indian Families Have Documented Succession Plans

items.summary: A cyber-attack targeting refrigerators and freezers forced dozens of supermarkets across several European countries to dump large quantities of spoiled food. Belgium and Luxemburg saw the worst damage, with 40 Delhaize supermarkets affected, while incidents also occurred in stores across Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. In a Hoeilaart branch near Brussels, frozen pizzas and ice cream were found among rubbish. The damaged store estimated costs at more than €100,000 (£83,500).
items.title: European supermarkets discard food after freezer cyber-attack

items.summary: German news magazine Der Spiegel reported that Apple sent spyware threat warnings to members of a delegation accompanying Chancellor Friedrich Merz on his recent trip to Singapore, Japan and South Korea. The alerts reached ministry staff and journalists as well. Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said the federal government is taking the incident very seriously while authorities investigate possible device compromise.
items.title: Apple Warns German Officials of Possible Spyware Breach After Merz Asia Trip

items.summary: Oracle filed Monday plans to raise $20 billion through stock and bond sales, seeking $10 billion each in common stock and senior notes. The company says proceeds may fund capital expenditures, debt repayments or future investments, with neither offering priced at filing. This follows an Oct. 28 investor day cap of $20 billion in fundraising through fiscal 2030. Oracle shares fell about 4.5% after the announcement.
items.title: Oracle Sells $20 Billion in Stock and Bonds for AI Growth

items.summary: President Donald Trump notified Congress he intends to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) preferential trade programme, effective 1 January 2027. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found both countries engaged in practices inconsistent with eligibility requirements. The administration cited barriers to trade, national security concerns, corruption, human rights issues, and strained relations between Washington and the two nations.
items.title: Trump Notifies Congress of Removing Rwanda and South Africa from AGOA Trade Program

items.summary: The United States Trade Representative announced Monday that Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) duty-free trade deal, citing practices inconsistent with eligibility criteria. The exclusions take effect January 1. Any removal requires 60 days' notice to Congress.
items.title: US Excludes South Africa and Rwanda From AGOA Trade Deal

items.summary: A last-minute endorsement by Democrat Haley Stevens of Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers has drawn sharp condemnation from fellow Democrats, who call it a betrayal after she was disinvited from Abdul El-Sayed's campaign over an advertisement. Schumer called it 'a despicable betrayal,' while Pelosi and Zohran Mamdani echoed the outrage; several staff members resigned in protest. Stevens declined to explain her reasoning on CNN Sunday but defended it Monday, comparing herself to John Fetterman. Meanwhile, Rogers and Trump praised her choice. El-Sayed's campaign raised more than $2.4m, a record, while Stevens' side reported over 26,000 contributors in one day.
items.title: Michigan Democrats condemn Haley Stevens for endorsing Mike Rogers

items.summary: Downing Street says Andy Burnham will ask countries affected by Britain’s role in slavery to help shape an expected formal apology, arguing their input is indispensable. He plans a structured dialogue at the Chogm summit in Antigua and Barbuda starting Tuesday, rather than deciding unilaterally. No 10 ruled out reparations but signalled debt restructuring talks; Buckingham Palace was told about Burnham’s comments amid claims they may have embarrassed King Charles.
items.title: Burnham Seeks Commonwealth Input on Historic Apology

items.summary: A short ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region has ended, according to a report noting that the pause offered residents of a besieged frontline city some relief from Russian drones that usually hunt and kill civilians there. Audio commentary on the situation is scheduled for later today.
items.title: Ceasefire in Kherson Region Ends After Brief Respite

items.summary: Two Tacuru officials in Mato Grosso do Sul were suspended after allegedly sending WhatsApp messages threatening to poison the water supply used by Guarani-Kaiowá people. The Ministry of the Federal Public Ministry (MPF) reported a 20-day suspension, but activists argue it is insufficient. Matias Benno Rempel called the threat rooted in concrete violence against Indigenous peoples, while Minister Eloy Terena pledged to combat all forms of violence.
items.title: Brazil Suspends Two Officials Over Threats to Poison Indigenous Water Supply

items.summary: At least 26 people were killed when Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, southern Zaporizhzhia region. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin said nine 3,000kg aerial bombs struck the village, injuring five and leaving 27 initially reported missing. President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack "utterly horrific" and later said 26 people were known to have died, following earlier tolls of 18 from himself and 24 confirmed by Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS.
items.title: Zelensky Condemns Russian Strike Killing 26 at Aid Centre

items.summary: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit overnight by cyber attacks broadcasting fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes, before the systems returned to control. Dr Melanie Garson of University College London told FRANCE 24 that these kinds of attacks are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust.
items.title: Expert Says Emergency Alert Hacking Aims To Undermine Government Trust

items.summary: North Korea dismissed U.S. claims that it was behind the cryptocurrency heist from Binance as 'absurd rhetoric,' according to state agency KCNA, which quoted Kim Yo Jong on Tuesday. The FBI had accused North Korea of stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets.
items.title: North Korea Rejects US Accusations Over Binance Heist

items.summary: The US is set to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), ending 26 years of duty-free market access. On Monday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said President Donald Trump intends to terminate both countries starting in January 2027, citing trade barriers and security concerns without specific examples. South Africa, AGOA's largest beneficiary with $1.7 billion (€1.5 billion) exported under the program in 2025, says exports make up only about 10% of its US sales. Rwanda faces pressure over alleged ties to the M23 rebel group.
items.title: US Drops South Africa and Rwanda From Duty-Free Trade Program

items.summary: ABC Sport's live blog opens Melbourne Cup Day, naming British colt Hopewell Rock as favourite for the 166th running of the race. The four-year-old begins its sixth career start among 24 runners in Ciaron Maher's record seven-horse field. Rain over the previous 24 hours left Flemington rated Soft 5.
items.title: Hopewell Rock Favourites as Melbourne Cup Day Opens at Flemington

items.summary: At the 2026 U.N. Biodiversity Conference in Armenia (COP17), Indigenous peoples and local communities strengthened their role in decision-making of the Convention on Biological Diversity through full operationalization of its Subsidiary body on Article 8(j). Delegates agreed to represent these communities via organizations operating in their countries, dropping mention of seven sociocultural regions. Jennifer Corpuz called it historic; Canada expressed disappointment with related language.
items.title: Indigenous Groups Gain Formal Role in Biodiversity Treaty at COP17

items.summary: Customers across Australia received scam messages after a data leak involving third-party booking provider RMS exposed names, bookings and contact details nationwide. Victims in Western Australia's Kimberley were targeted with phishing texts containing accurate trip details to steal payment information. RMS contained the unauthorised activity yesterday; its chief executive Adam Seskis said scams have become increasingly sophisticated but confirmed card details were not breached. Cybersecurity lecturer Brianna O'Shea called it 'just the tip of the iceberg.' Hotels advised guests not to respond or share card details.
items.title: RMS Data Leak Fuels Sophisticated Scam Messages Across Australia

items.summary: A decade after polls badly missed in the 2016 presidential election, forecasters project a large Democratic lead heading into the November midterm elections. Surveys of the generic congressional ballot show Democrats ahead by eight points, similar to their 2018 margin, yet races in states like Texas and Ohio fall within the margin of error. Charles Franklin of Marquette Law School explains that polling errors tend to move together nationally, so a single bias could swing many contests at once. He cautions against treating polls as predictions, advising readers simply to be uncertain.
items.title: Pollsters Warn Midterm 'Blue Wave' Could Fade or Surge

items.summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby arrived Monday, November 2 at his mother's home in Hull after a journey spanning roughly five decades. The former paratrooper set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, in November 1998 to reach his mother without conventional transport. He reunited with family he had been away from for nearly three decades and met his son Adam and granddaughter for the first time.
items.title: Karl Bushby Completes Two-Decade Journey Home After Circling the World

items.summary: The British government set out a tougher earned settlement model on Monday, doubling the qualifying period for indefinite leave to remain from five years to 10 years for most workers. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood confirmed the change in parliament, while high earners and some public service staff can still settle sooner or after five years. Care workers earning £25,000 (roughly €29,900) are exempt from the extension. Andy Burnham said Britain had lost control of immigration after Brexit.
items.title: UK Government Doubles Settlement Waiting Period Under New Earned Model

items.summary: On the eve of US midterm elections, President Donald Trump's administration is seeking a Supreme Court injunction to sideline over 20,000 mail-in ballots in California, claiming non-US citizens are attempting to vote. The Justice Department, run by former personal attorney Todd Blanche, says it has a list documenting alleged ineligible voters compiled by the Department of Homeland Security. A district court judge rejected an earlier request, warning singling out ballots would harm voter trust.
items.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Block California Ballots

items.summary: An explosion followed by a fire at Metafrique Steel metal processing company in Douala's Bassa industrial zone on Monday morning left at least four people dead and sixteen others seriously injured. Emergency services found the bodies, and wounded workers were taken to Douala General Hospital with burns covering much of their skin. The Littoral Region Governor condemned safety failures after a May fire and raised possible shutdowns.
items.title: Cameroon Steel Plant Explosion Kills Four, Injures Many

items.summary: Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the July-September quarter, with much of its net loss from non-cash valuation charges. Its amended IPO filing disclosed spending commitments of approximately $895 billion toward computing infrastructure, including $70 billion due before September 2027. The company is considering raising around $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion as it tests investor appetite for AI investments.
items.title: Anthropic's Revenue Surge and AI Spending Ahead of IPO

items.summary: PIB Fact Check has labelled a widely shared message as fake, clarifying that the Reserve Bank of India issued no announcement warning of a shortage of Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 50 notes ahead of Diwali. The viral circular, dated October 27, 2026, claimed inadequate supply during the festive season and urged people to use UPI, cards and net banking instead of cash. It also suggested printing was being reduced as part of a less-cash economy move. After the message circulated on WhatsApp, PIB shared its clarification on X, urging people to verify information against official RBI announcements before believing or sharing such messages.
items.title: Press Information Bureau Fact Check Debunks Viral Fake RBI Circular on Small-Denomination Notes

items.summary: The Supreme Court refused Monday to urgently list a plea challenging steep domestic air fare rises during Diwali and asked the Centre to design a capping mechanism. A bench was informed regulation is still pending, then turned down the request. Advocate Abhinav argued fares rose 700%, breaching Article 14. The bench said "Don't travel by air." The Centre earlier told the court new rules under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 would appear within two weeks.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Urgent Plea on Air Fares

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench kept the window open for bursting green firecrackers in Delhi and the national capital region on Nov 7-8, permitting two time slots between 6am-7am and 8pm-10pm. The court stressed that religious practices remain subject to constitutional restrictions against pollution and health hazards. It directed authorities to ensure polluting crackers stay out of bounds and take punitive action against violators.
items.title: Supreme Court Keeps Green Firecrackers Allowed on Diwali in Delhi

items.summary: US air safety investigators said there are early indications the Learjet 60 that crashed near Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday had broken up before impact, killing all nine people aboard and injuring at least one person on the ground. National Transportation Safety Board Member Tom Chapman told reporters they were still seeking to determine whether parts such as the horizontal stabilizer came off beforehand, noting adverse weather remained a major focus of the investigation. Preliminary data from Flightradar24 showed the aircraft began a rapid descent around 12:48 p.m., with its vertical rate eventually exceeding 32,000 feet per minute. The cause has not been determined.
items.title: NTSB Flags Possible Breakup in Fatal Florida Learjet Crash

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspended licences of 19 food business operators, including a super distributor of Patanjali Ayurved, during a festive-season drive. The agency said it seized around 3. 53 lakh kg of food articles valued at Rs 9. 01 crore from 114 establishments across seven divisions on suspicion of adulteration and hygiene violations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Among the stock was 2,279. 7 litres of Patanjali cow ghee worth Rs 20. 20 lakh seized from M/s Divya Mahavitarak in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The drive also led to 13 FIRs, 16 arrests and seven sealed establishments.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Seizes Rs 9 Crore of Food Stock

items.summary: An Australian couple who left winemaking in South Australia's Riverland region have restored their Murtho property to native bush. The three-year project covered around 14 hectares and finished in 2026 with more than 3,000 seedlings planted. Supported by the Murraylands and Riverland Landscape Board and Trees For Life, it aims to rebuild habitat for the vulnerable regent parrot, whose South Australian population is estimated at fewer than 400 breeding pairs. Four generations of the family took part in planting.
items.title: Australian couple restore vineyard land, aiding regent parrot recovery

items.summary: Russian air strikes killed at least 24 people in a humanitarian aid center near Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, Ukraine's authorities said. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the double-tap strike as 'utterly horrific.' Bloomberg could not independently verify details. The attack adds to rising civilian casualties: UN figures show an 85% jump in September deaths versus last year.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Russian Strike on Aid Center Kills at Least 24

items.summary: The Shawn Carter Foundation, founded by Jay-Z and his mother Dr Gloria Carter in 2003, says it has made more than 2,700 scholarship awards since its inception. According to the foundation’s newsletter figures shared through a report by Parade on Yahoo!, 324 of those awards were given during the 2025-26 academic year. The National Scholarship Fund supports students from admission through graduation with up to $15,000 for tuition and living costs. Recipients are expected to take part in community service and mentoring younger applicants. The foundation describes itself as a family-led effort aimed at helping motivated students who lack financial means pursue education beyond high school.
items.title: Jay-Z Foundation Awards Over 2,700 Scholarships

items.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall on the south Andhra Pradesh coast early Tuesday with sustained winds of 100-110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph, per the India Meteorological Department. Around 2,000 people had been evacuated from vulnerable coastal areas, while authorities planned to move approximately 30,000 more to safer locations, as reported by PTI. The storm arrived less than a week after Cyclone Arnab affected eastern coastal regions. Heavy rainfall and possible storm surge of around 1 to 1.5 metres prompted widespread alerts across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and neighbouring states, with flights and trains disrupted ahead of landfall. Tamil Nadu sent NDRF teams comprising 90 personnel plus electricity department staff numbering 500 to support relief efforts in the affected areas.Officials directed officials to remain on high alert for rescue, relief and restoration work as damage assessments began across power networks, roads, houses and crops.
items.title: Cyclone Murasu Landfalls in Andhra Pradesh, Thousands Evacuated
